records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] max_processes is computed with `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so passing flusher_processes=0 (the only falsy int) silently degrades to one-process-per-shard instead of an error. An operator typo of --flusher-processes=0 (or an options value of 0) spawns one process per shard rather than failing loudly, the opposite of the intent of a cap, and only bites when shard counts are high enough to matter for resource usage.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the cap is set as `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. Because `0` is falsy, passing `flusher_processes=0` (possible via the new `--flusher-processes` click option, which is just `type=int` with no lower-bound validation) will silently fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e., effectively removing the cap and allowing one process per shard (`self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`). That matches the finding’s concern about an operator typo causing the opposite of the intended resource cap.

The `if not process: continue` guard at the top of the loop is also dead (dict values are always truthy objects), masking that this path was never exercised.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Metric tag key is inconsistent: wait_produce uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} while produce and segment_size_bytes use tags={"shard": shard_tag}. Dashboards/alerts grouping spans.buffer.flusher.* by shard will split wait_produce into a separate tag dimension ('shards') from its sibling metrics ('shard'), breaking per-shard aggregation and alert queries on the touched metrics path.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the metric tags are inconsistent for per-shard metrics: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` both use the key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This creates a different tag dimension for `wait_produce` than its sibling `spans.buffer.flusher.*` metrics, which will break grouping/queries expecting `shard`.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] join() shares a single deadline across sequential per-process wait loops, so the first slow process consumes the entire budget and all remaining processes are terminated while still alive. During consumer shutdown with a short timeout and multiple flusher processes, every process after the first is terminated mid-flush the moment its loop is entered, dropping in-flight segment flushes to Redis-backed loss and defeating the 'flush while next_step shuts down' design the comment describes.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, a single `deadline` is computed once (`deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None`) and then processes are handled sequentially. The wait loop for each process is `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time()): time.sleep(0.1)`. On loaded CI runners the background thread may not poll Redis within 100ms, producing intermittent failures of the core consumer test — the reviewer who introduced multiprocess concurrency converted a deterministic test into a timing-dependent one without an acceptance note.
records.rationale: The finding claims the test now depends on a fixed `time.sleep(0.1)` wait, but in `test_basic` the diff explicitly patches `time.sleep` to a no-op: `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. Therefore the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not actually wait 100ms (or any time) and cannot introduce the stated timing dependency on loaded CI runners.

records.issue_text: [BUG] An unvalidated --flusher-processes value of 0 (or negative) causes num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards)) to be 0 or negative, and the round-robin assignment `i % self.num_processes` raises ZeroDivisionError (or negative modulo misassigns shards) at flusher construction, crashing the consumer at startup with an unhandled exception instead of a clean config error. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the deadline expires, so any processes after the one being waited on never reach their terminate() call and leak. During consumer shutdown with a short join timeout and N flusher processes, up to N-1 spawn processes (holding Redis connections and producer futures with unflushed segment data) survive past shutdown; on consumer restart the same shards get a second live flusher, racing on Redis segment claims until the orphan exits.
records.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the new per-process loop breaks entirely when the shared deadline expires: `if remaining_time <= 0: break`. Because `process.terminate()` is called inside the loop after waiting on each process, any processes that appear later in `self.processes.items()` will never reach the terminate call once the `break` happens, leaving them running past shutdown.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In submit(), the backpressure loop calls `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")` once per unhealthy process before raising, so with N backpressured processes the counter is incremented N times per rejected message. The backpressure metric's rate is multiplied by the number of stuck processes, distorting dashboards that gauge how long or how often backpressure engages; operators correlating the metric with actual Kafka lag or Redis memory see inflated counts under the multi-process configuration this diff introduces.
records.rationale:
The diff shows `submit()` increments the backpressure metric and immediately raises on the *first* backpressured process encountered, so it cannot increment N times per rejected message. Specifically:

```py
for backpressure_since in self.process_backpressure_since.values():
    if (...):
        metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")
        raise MessageRejected()
```

Because `raise MessageRejected()` exits the function, the loop cannot continue to increment the metric for additional processes in the same call.
